newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand bond yields end higher but tone firm.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand bond yields end higher but tone firm.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD (PCT)
90-DAY BILLS (SEP) 92.10 (PREV 92.07) 90-DAYS 8.21 (PREV 8.28)
OVERNIGHT CASH 8.15 PCT (PREV 8.10) US 5-YR 6.12 (PREV 6.11)
RBNZ MCI NZ/MCI 744.25 (PREV 744.28) Reuters NZ MCI -78 vs -81
New Zealand bond yields closed slightly bid on Wednesday after yields had risen earlier in the session.

Yields in the short end of the market closed lower in response to the firmer currency. Dealers said the short end was dollar watching. One said that bill yields rose through the session as the currency slipped.
The Monetary Conditions Index ended little changed at 78 basis points easier than the Reserve Bank's desired level and dealers said 70-90 points easier appeared to be something of a new comfort zone.
The 90-day bills were hitting resistance at 8.15 percent. They ended at 8.21 percent after being bought at 8.13 percent in the opening.
Dealers said there was still a considerable gap between physical and futures prices and that would have to narrow.
Bond yields opened higher as profit takers from a NZ$600 million issue sold the market.
"They was a little bit of over-hedging and certainly some bonds came back onshore," said one dealer.
However, the bids reemerged later in the session as traders expect New Zealand bonds to perform relatively well.
"It depends in a large measure on the U.S. and also on the currency," said one dealer.

"I would have thought that up here we may look like a bit of a buy especially on the spread to Aussie. A lot depends on people getting comfortable with the kiwi dollar and, especially in the short end and the mid-curve bonds, the currency is the key thing people are focussing on," he said.
